parsed.explanation: Combined regime: a buggery statute (up to 10 years) is on the books but no documented visitor arrests under it. Police fail to protect LGBT people and leak incident details, and a 2013 mob killing of a gender-nonconforming teen went uninvestigated. Custody is the most severe documented exposure: identity-targeted violence in overcrowded prisons, isolation, and reported corrective rape, with no gender-recognition framework to guide placement. Entry screening and gender-marker treatment for visitors are not documented. Public opinion is consistently hostile, though resort enclaves report few incidents. Most documents are dated (2004–2013), and the most recent incident is from January 2023. Rated as High Risk, driven by custody exposure and police non-intervention.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented treatment of transgender visitors at entry, marker checks, or visa screening. A 2018 entry ban concerned a foreign anti-gay pastor, not a trans visitor.
entry_documents.interaction: Unknown whether foreign-issued documents are questioned; if outed at entry, the sodomy statute and hostile climate would carry forward.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented identity-targeted violence in pretrial lockups and prisons, including a 2023 video of a beating and scalding attack. Isolation and corrective rape of lesbians are reported. Overcrowding runs at 3x capacity. No gender-recognition framework informs accommodation.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented protective housing or specialised policy.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Once detained, state custody is the exposure; wardens and inmates both reported as perpetrators, and complaints to the prison system rarely produce recourse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No national facility-access or bathroom rule documented for visitors. Prison housing is not explicitly by birth sex, but no gender-recognition framework is documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Not documented whether national prison rules override local custody or hospital practice.

care_services.exposure: Documented harassment of gay and lesbian patients by hospital and prison staff (2012). Documented service exclusion for trans users of the domestic health system (2023 survey).
care_services.protection: No documented working care protection for trans people.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing care would meet the same hospital staff; the 2023 survey concerns residents, so visitor-specific care denial is not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: The sodomy statute remains in force. Officials and musicians have incited hostility. The 2023 report records that the state barred legal gender registration. Police harassment of trans women is documented in public-health literature.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: A tourism director said gay visitors are welcome (2019); this is a statement, not an operative protection.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official signals conflict: a welcome statement sits beside a city block of an LGBT venue and police disclaiming protection.

minors_guardians.exposure: A gender-nonconforming 16-year-old was killed by a mob in 2013 and the case remains unsolved. Students aged 18–29 bore most documented violence. No documentation of guardian-specific rules.
minors_guardians.interaction: Minors and guardians travelling together face the same street and custody exposure; no separate rule is documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Vigilante and mob violence documented (2004, 2006, 2012, 2013). Campus violence documented. Police leak details, fail to investigate, and do not intervene during attacks. Majority of LGBTQ respondents report public homophobic violence (2013). Counts lack denominators.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Resort bubbles are reported as low-incident. Some university working groups on bullying.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police non-response removes recourse for outed visitors; the resort-bubble protection covers only enclaves.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No functioning remedy documented: police fail to investigate, prison complaints bring retaliation, activist litigation has failed, and LGBT organisations are underground or closed.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Documented but limited: a 2013 Constitutional Court and pending appellate litigation; no operative relief documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse in the rubric's sense is absent; litigation is not shown to change outcomes for trans people.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A has a documented universal exclusion register and airline enforcement, which this dossier does not document. This case has no documented border exclusion, so it sits above 0.35-A on entry, but its custody and mob violence are more severe than the detention-and-release pattern in 0.35-B.

0.25-C documents birth-sex male-block housing and a cross-dressing arrest statute. This dossier documents prison identity violence and no gender-recognition housing rule, but not a birth-sex housing mandate or cross-dressing statute. Its custody exposure is similar, its statutory exposure lighter, so it sits close to 0.25-C.

0.15-A documents routine arrests of visitors, custodial beatings with courts failing, and an unused capital clause. This dossier documents custody violence and non-intervention, but no visitor arrests and no capital pathway. It is clearly higher than 0.15-A.

parsed.synthesis: The sodomy statute and hostile opinion create a standing exposure. Police non-intervention and uninvestigated killings remove recourse, so an outed visitor has little protection on the street. Custody is the most severe documented exposure: identity-targeted violence, isolation, and corrective rape with no gender-recognition housing guidance. Entry and facility rules for visitors are undocumented, so they are not scored as exposures. Most incidents are dated and no visitor-specific cases are recorded, which keeps the rating in the High Risk band rather than the Severe band.
